name: English as a Second Language ESL Level 5
subject: English As a Second Language and English Literacy Development
subject_group: English As a Second Language and English Literacy Development
description: This course provides students with the skills and strategies they need to make the transition to college and university preparation courses in English and other secondary school disciplines. Students will be encouraged to develop independence in a range of academic tasks. They will participate in debates and lead classroom workshops; read and interpret literary works and academic texts; write essays, narratives, and reports; and apply a range of learning strategies and research skills effectively. Students will further develop their ability to respond critically to print and media texts.

overall_expectations.title: Developing Media Knowledge and Skills
overall_expectations.describer: By the end of this course, students will:
overall_expectations.text: demonstrate an understanding of, interpret, and create a variety of media texts
overall_expectations.text_html: demonstrate an understanding of, interpret, and create a variety of media texts

specific_expectations.text: view, read, and listen to a variety of media texts, and explain some ways in which they influence society (e.g., how the ideas and images in various media affect social and cultural norms, lifestyles, and gender roles)
specific_expectations.text_html: view, read, and listen to a variety of media texts, and explain some ways in which they influence society (e.g., how the ideas and images in various media affect social and cultural norms, lifestyles, and gender roles)

elaborations.text: Which groups in Canada are represented most positively and which are most negatively represented in ads on television and in magazines?
elaborations.text_html: • Which groups in Canada are represented most positively and which are most negatively represented in ads on television and in magazines?

specific_expectations.text: analyse coverage of current local, national, or global issues in a variety of media texts to identify subjective approaches and types of bias
specific_expectations.text_html: analyse coverage of current local, national, or global issues in a variety of media texts to identify subjective approaches and types of bias

elaborations.text: In this news report about a conflict between two countries, does the reporter favour one side over the other? Give support for your opinion.
elaborations.text_html: • In this news report about a conflict between two countries, does the reporter favour one side over the other? Give support for your opinion.

specific_expectations.text: create a variety of media texts for specific purposes and audiences, and explain how the purpose and audience influenced their design decisions and language choice (e.g., a class newspaper or pamphlet to inform parents about the achievements and activities of students in the class; an advertising campaign to appeal to specific consumer groups; a review of a television program, film, or artistic performance to encourage teenagers or adults to see it)
